title: Using OS.add_logger() causes exported projects to segfault on exit
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in 4.5 beta.4 and beta.3

### System information

Fedora Linux 42 (KDE Plasma Desktop Edition)

### Issue description

Creating a custom logger class that inherits from `Logger` and registering it using `OS.add_logger()` will cause the exported project to segfault after you close it.

```GDScript
func _ready() -> void:
	var my_logger: MyLogger = MyLogger.new()
	OS.add_logger(my_logger)
```

It does not matter if the custom class is empty, overrides the virtual `Logger` methods or implements new methods. The custom logger itself works correctly otherwise.

Below are the `--verbose` logs of the MRP exported without debug for `Linux x86_64` using default settings.

I should mention that at first, I only got a simple segfault with no details. I decided to also test beta.3 and after I installed the templates, I got bigger and more beautiful errors. I can't really download every other templates to check, so I hope this will be good enough.
The custom logger is completely empty below, though I have tested multiple versions with no difference:
```GDScript
class_name MyLogger extends Logger
```

Using beta.4 export templates (before installing beta.3 export templates):
```
Segmentation fault (core dumped).
```

Run the exported project, and close the window.
